page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Running head at top, with the page number at top right. Marginal notes in the right margin. A woodcut initial opens the chapter. A single "O" sits centred at the foot.

main_text.p: cuius tota est anima. Ex his perspicuum est, stirpes & animantia commune principium habere, nempe animam, sine quo nihil horū est, quod viuere possit.
main_text.head: CAP. V.
Generalis definitio animæ.
main_text.p: C.1.l.2[?]de ani-ma.Osthæc quidnā anima sit, & eius communis ratio, explicandū nobis est. Itaque aut substantia est, aut accidens: quandoquidem eorum, quæ esse dicuntur plura non sunt genera. Sed anima accidens esse non potest, quoniā omnium animati corporis functionum facultatūmque illa fons est & principium: Anima igitur substantia est. Sed quod substatiæ genus sit, rursus quærendum est. Substantiarum enim alia materies est, & τοῦ[?] po-testate, quæ per se rei alicuius singularis naturam non habet: alia forma & species, quaquidem iā res singularis est, quoniā ipsius rei ratio existit, & perfectio. Tertium substantiæ genus ex materia constat & specie, ac naturale corpus est. Huiusmodi autem corporis duplex genus habetur, vnum quod eorum est, quæ viuunt: alterum aliorum, quæ inanimata sunt. At quæ viuunt ea nutriuntur, crescunt, & minuuntur: quoniam nutritio, augmentatio, & imminutio ab anima fiunt. Quare anima substantia sit, necesse est, perinde ac forma corporis naturalis, organici.

page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated letter spanning three lines; I read the word as "Osthæc" with the initial joined, but its exact letter is unclear. The Greek word after "&" is uncertain (marked [?]); it appears to be τὸ δυνάμει ("potestate"). The margin note at the top right reads "C.1.l.2" with the last letters doubtful. Printed irregularities left as printed: "substatiæ", "animāti", "quoniā", "iā". The "O" at the foot is taken as a gathering signature but could be an ornament.
